sq.q: \(\text{State the one-dimensional wave equation for a vibrating string and list the physical assumptions made in its derivation.}\)
answer: \(\text{Wave equation: } \frac{\partial^2 y}{\partial t^2} = c^2 \frac{\partial^2 y}{\partial x^2}\)
\(\text{1. String is homogeneous and perfectly elastic.}\)

sq.q: \(\text{Using separation of variables, solve } \frac{\partial^2 y}{\partial t^2} = c^2 \frac{\partial^2 y}{\partial x^2} \text{ and obtain the ODEs for } X(x) \text{ and } T(t). \text{ Discuss the three cases for the separation constant.}\)
answer: \(\text{Case 1: } k>0, k=\lambda^2: X''-\lambda^2 X=0, T''-\lambda^2 c^2 T=0.\)
\(\text{Case 2: } k<0, k=-\lambda^2: X''+\lambda^2 X=0, T''+\lambda^2 c^2 T=0.\)
\(\text{The solutions for each case are exponential, trigonometric, or linear.}\)

lq.q: \(\text{Using separation of variables, derive the three possible solutions of the one-dimensional}\\ \text{wave equation } \frac{\partial^2 y}{\partial t^2} = c^2 \frac{\partial^2 y}{\partial x^2}.\\ \text{Explain why the trigonometric solution is most suitable for a vibrating string problem with fixed ends.}\)
answer: Step Marks \(\text{Assume \(y(x,t)=X(x)T(t)\). Substitute into PDE to get \(XT'' = c^2X''T\).}\) (1 Mark) \(\text{Separate variables: \(\dfrac{X''}{X} = \dfrac{T''}{(c^2T)} = k\) (constant).}\) (2 Marks) \(\text{Case \(k > 0\) (\(k=\lambda^2\)): \(X'' - \lambda^2X=0\), \(T'' - \lambda^2c^2T=0\) \(\Rightarrow\) solutions: \(X = Ae^{\lambda x}+Be^{-\lambda x}\), \(T = Ce^{\lambda ct}+De^{-\lambda ct}\).}\) (2 Marks) \(\text{Case \(k < 0\) (\(k=-\lambda^2\)): \(X'' + \lambda^2X=0\), \(T'' + \lambda^2c^2T=0\) \(\Rightarrow\) solutions: \(X = A \cos(\lambda x) + B \sin(\lambda x)\), \(T = C \cos(\lambda c t) + D \sin(\lambda c t)\).}\) (2 Marks) \(\text{Case \(k = 0\): \(X''=0\), \(T''=0\) \(\Rightarrow\) \(X = Ax+B\), \(T = Ct+D\).}\) (1 Mark) \(\text{For vibrating string with fixed ends, boundary conditions \(y(0,t)=0\), \(y(l,t)=0\) require periodic solutions in space.}\) (2 Marks) \(\text{Trigonometric solutions (sine and cosine) are periodic and satisfy fixed end conditions naturally after applying BCs.}\) (2 Marks) Exponential and linear solutions do not represent bounded vibrations for a finite string. (2 Marks) Hence trigonometric form is suitable. (1 Mark)
